An image on a plane of the panel

Source: R/layers-texture.R
annotation_raster_3d.Rd

Lays an image on a plane of the 3D panel, such as a map on the floor or a photograph on a wall. The image is one textured face of the scene: it is foreshortened with the plane and hidden by what lies in front of it, and the raster backend and the view_3d() viewer sample it perspective correctly (see texture_3d()). Unlike ggplot2::annotation_raster(), which coord_3d() also draws this way on the floor, the image can stand on any axis plane.

Usage

annotation_raster_3d(
  raster,
  xmin = -Inf,
  xmax = Inf,
  ymin = -Inf,
  ymax = Inf,
  plane = "xy",
  at = -Inf,
  interpolate = TRUE,
  alpha = 1
)

Arguments

raster

An image accepted by texture_3d(), or a texture.

xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax

Image extent along the first and second axis of plane.

plane

Two distinct axis letters, such as "xy", "xz" or "yz", or "floor" for "xy".

at

Position on the remaining axis; -Inf and Inf place the image on the lower and upper box side (0 when no other layer trains that axis).

interpolate

Whether to interpolate between pixels, see texture_3d().

alpha

Opacity of the image.

Value

A ggplot2 layer.

Details

The image's horizontal direction runs along the first axis of plane from xmin to xmax, its vertical direction along the second axis from ymin to ymax; a reversed pair mirrors it. Infinite positions reach the sides of the panel box. The remaining axis is fixed at at.

See also

geom_raster_3d() for data on a regular grid, texture_3d().

Examples

logo <- matrix(grDevices::hcl.colors(12, "Zissou 1"), 3, 4)
d <- data.frame(x = runif(30), y = runif(30), z = runif(30))
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  annotation_raster_3d(logo, 0, 1, 0, 1, plane = "xz", at = Inf, interpolate = FALSE) +
  annotation_raster_3d(logo, 0, 1, 0, 1, plane = "floor") +
  geom_point_3d() +
  coord_3d()
